The Federal Aviation Administration issued certification for Boeing’s 737 MAX-10, marking a significant milestone in the return of the aircraft to commercial service [FAA issued certification](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/federal-aviation-administration-issues-certification-boeing-737-max-10). This action follows the agency’s adoption of a new airworthiness directive for certain Boeing airplanes, reinforcing safety protocols for the manufacturer’s fleet [FAA adopted directive](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21332/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes). Concurrently, the agency proposed a $351,000 civil penalty against Creamer Pilot Services for alleged unauthorized passenger-carrying operations, signaling continued enforcement of operational compliance standards [FAA proposed fine](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-proposes-351000-fine-against-creamer-pilot-services-alleged-unauthorized-passenger).

In the unmanned systems sector, the Federal Aviation Administration imposed a ban on unauthorized drones along the U.S.-Mexico border through 2027 to counter cartel threats [FAA imposed ban](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxNdDg1dDI4Mm9ZVWhPUWc5RWxadlR5dFZHR0JENjU5QmVXRDBSVWJmTGxidzJqYXVheTQzeEJVLUtST0lVeHFtaDJkRVBrcVI5bExHRTg5M3FNSGF0REtOb0o5S3dERk42OUoxZWFqdFVaemkxclh2US1HaHVLblE2ZjBvenVkRHFKckJwZGNNQ2pySXd0TVUtbjh4akhPVUJiRlE). This restriction reflects a broader trend of heightened airspace security measures, as the agency also restricted border drone operations to mitigate security risks [FAA restricted operations](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxPc1pjSzN4X2UteGJjMkRFdFFrYk13MHl5c1BGVmRma0NkZjJZc0tUZTVNaFdpMDg5TEx5QjdFTW03LUJnZHNmdFctX3BvNTJNcXZFYVgtZzdtcHdmOGFhWjc2X2NPbjI4c0dGMVNfNG5jQjNwMDdCRGpzbWVha05DQkJGSF92ZlJXNUV4c1o2SldrWlpHNUFpSmEwRks4MjNvUm5PVnpGS1JIeFlxM2g0MzJMU1RWTHpv). These actions underscore the administration’s focus on securing critical infrastructure and border regions against unauthorized aerial activity.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration audited 1,000 Cybercabs as Tesla targets a 2026 sale, intensifying regulatory scrutiny on autonomous vehicle deployments [NHTSA audited Cybercabs](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiggFBVV95cUxQbXJHT3o3VURFQWw1YlI0cVBnSDY3TFhCYkxVOV9NUzk2UlltbFg3UE9iY2pZU0gtY0w1ZnZpRlVvOHhEYVVYamdmNWhwMTBubjBWeGVndjBockMzSndFY2o5d2ZPaW1QcGt0YWhQUlZGWC1OSkRMSjRlRnRvZEJ2Q2Fn). The agency also opened a probe into Tesla robotaxis for speeding and ignoring school zones, highlighting ongoing safety concerns with self-driving technology [NHTSA opened probe](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMic0FVX3lxTE8zQThsSmRPZXVoOHRjRmt6QllXU1lQYkJuQ0o1ckdVX2lDbmg0Nk4yTnlyamxqU0lnanc2Qk1sdVJZMlFRUE1BN1lwSFZiVzl3U2NBWFBWN1I5VDA4cEZFUHBEdkNYb1JhLS0xbmtCNlduQ1E). Meanwhile, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration finalized a decision to renew and modify an exemption from hours-of-service prohibitions for railroad associations, adjusting operational flexibility for rail operators [FMCSA finalized decision](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/21/2026-21488/hours-of-service-of-drivers-association-of-american-railroads-and-american-short-line-and-regional).

In advanced aviation, Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy announced the first-ever Special Airworthiness Market Survey Certificate for eVTOL aircraft, establishing a new regulatory pathway for electric vertical takeoff and landing vehicles [Secretary announced certificate](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-first-ever-special-airworthiness). This development supports the growing urban air mobility sector by providing a framework for market validation and certification. Additionally, the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Air Traffic Controllers Association reached a deal to provide air traffic controllers with a 2.8% pay increase, addressing workforce compensation issues within the agency [FAA reached deal](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-department-air-traffic-controller-union-announce-28-pay-increase).
